As a young man I remember hearing a popular slogan about faith: “Faith begins when reason ends.” As a young Christian, I thought it was a great life slogan. As I mature in my walk with Jesus, I look back on this particular slogan and shake my head. I can think of no better way to misrepresent faith than by claiming it exists apart from reason.

One simple reason for rejecting this view is because it misrepresents faith. A quick search on Google turns up this definition of faith: “complete trust or confidence in someone or something.” We use this definition all the time. I might tell you I have faith in my wife, I have faith in my employer to give me a paycheck, or I have no faith in alcohol to give me a good time. This is the same way the Bible defines faith.

Hebrews 11:1 affirms that faith is “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” Biblical faith is simply a state of mind that has confidence and trust in the Lord. I have confidence that I will one day walk on the new Earth, and I have confidence that the Holy Spirit is working in the hearts of Christians. My confidence is based on, not apart from, reason. The more Jesus shows himself trustworthy, the more I trust (have confidence in) Him.

One aspect of Christ’s dependability is His word. The Old Testament was written by prophets and leaders who correctly predicted future events and ruled nations. The New Testament was written by Apostles or people that were closely associated with the apostles. We have more manuscripts of the Bible than any other work in antiquity. The Bible gives an honest portrayal of its heroes and correctly describes ancient leaders and places. In short, I trust in the Bible because it stands alone above all other books in terms of its authorship, preservation, honesty, and accuracy. The more I read it and read about it, the more my faith—and trust—increases.

Luke bases his whole Gospel on the premise that more knowledge gives more faith. He begins his book with this introduction: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled [or been surely believed] among us, just as they were handed down to us by those who from the first were eyewitnesses and servants of the word. With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught. –Luke 1:1-4. (NIV)

The apostle Paul argues that faith in God is so grounded in reality that no one has a legitimate claim against God’s existence. He writes, The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse –Romans 1:18-20. (NIV)

Knowledge of nature builds my faith in Jesus. Scripture teaches that God created all life in six days, that there was a global flood, and that animals produce after their own kind. All across our earth, the rocks cry out their testimony of the global flood. People have uncovered billions of fossils—mostly marine animals—in rock layers that were laid down by water. Animals too, live out what the Bible teaches about kinds. We can observe animals changing all around us. They change sizes, colors, and eating habits. Fish in caves lose their ability to see. Birds’ beaks adjust to the environment. In all this intricate change, all animals exist within the Biblical framework of their own kind. Sharks remain sharks; frogs remain frogs; iguanas remain iguanas; and gibbons remain gibbons. The more I learn and observe about nature, the more my faith (confidence) increases.

In some discussions of faith, it is natural for the words of Jesus to come up. After His resurrection, Jesus visits Thomas and tells him, …Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed –John 20:29. (ESV) From this, it is tempting to define faith as “believing without seeing.” That would be missing the point. I’m not claiming any superiority to Thomas, but he should have believed without seeing Jesus. All the evidence pointed to it. First, his good friends, who had proved themselves trustworthy, said Jesus was alive. Second, Jesus had plainly said He would be resurrected (see Matthew 16:21). Third, Jesus had already proven He was divine by His ability to raise the dead, control the weather, heal the sick, and multiply food. Thomas had all he needed to believe Jesus rose from the dead. Yet, he went against all reasoning and said he needed more evidence.

When confronted with the resurrected Christ, Thomas repented of his disbelief and followed Christ into martyrdom. Unfortunately, the spirit of disbelief in the face of evidence still lingers in our world. Atheists claim, in spite of all evidence to the contrary, that life can come from nothing. They claim, without any evidence, that fish turned into frogs. They blindly cling to various theories such as: The Big Bang, Punctuated Equilibrium, and Descent with Modification. They have NO workable evidence, yet they still claim to base all their thoughts on observable, repeatable reality. Christians, who with good intentions, tell them that faith begins where reason ends, unwittingly play right into their hands. This world does not need a social media definition of faith. They need to see faith for what it is: confidence in the living God based firmly in reason.

Юношей я помню, как услышал популярный лозунг о вере: «Вера начинается там, где заканчивается разум». Будучи молодым христианином, я считал его замечательным жизненным девизом. Теперь, когда я взрослею в своем хождении с Иисусом, я вспоминаю этот лозунг и качаю головой. Мне не приходит в голову более верного способа исказить смысл веры, чем утверждать, будто она существует отдельно от разума.

Есть простая причина отвергнуть этот взгляд: он искажает смысл веры. Быстрый поиск в Google выдает такое определение веры: «полное доверие или уверенность в ком-либо или чем-либо». Мы постоянно пользуемся этим определением. Я могу сказать, что доверяю своей жене, уверен, что работодатель выплатит мне зарплату, или что я не надеюсь получить удовольствие от алкоголя. Библия определяет веру точно так же.

В Послании к Евреям 11:1 говорится, что вера — это «уверенность в том, на что надеемся, и убежденность в том, чего не видим». Библейская вера — это просто состояние ума, исполненное уверенности и доверия Господу. Я уверен, что однажды буду ходить по новой Земле, и уверен, что Святой Дух действует в сердцах христиан. Моя уверенность основана на разуме, а не существует вне его. Чем явственнее Иисус показывает Свою надежность, тем больше я доверяю Ему (тем больше уверен в Нем).

Одно из проявлений надежности Христа — Его слово. Ветхий Завет был написан пророками и вождями, которые верно предсказывали будущие события и управляли народами. Новый Завет был написан апостолами или людьми, тесно связанными с апостолами. Рукописей Библии у нас больше, чем любого другого произведения древности. Библия правдиво изображает своих героев и точно описывает древних правителей и места. Короче говоря, я доверяю Библии, потому что по авторству, сохранности, честности и точности она не имеет себе равных среди всех прочих книг. Чем больше я читаю ее и узнаю о ней, тем больше укрепляется моя вера — и доверие.

Лука строит все свое Евангелие на предпосылке, что большее знание укрепляет веру. Он начинает свою книгу такими словами: Многие уже брались составлять повествования о событиях, которые совершились среди нас [или в которых мы твердо убеждены], как передали нам бывшие с самого начала очевидцами и служителями слова. Поэтому и я, тщательно исследовав все с самого начала, решил написать для тебя, досточтимый Феофил, последовательное повествование, чтобы ты знал достоверность того, чему был научен. —Луки 1:1-4. (NIV)

Апостол Павел утверждает, что вера в Бога настолько укоренена в реальности, что никто не может обоснованно отрицать существование Бога. Он пишет: Ибо гнев Божий открывается с неба на всякое нечестие и неправду людей, которые неправдою подавляют истину. Ведь то, что можно знать о Боге, очевидно для них, потому что Бог сделал это очевидным для них. Ибо от сотворения мира невидимое Божье — Его вечная сила и Божество — ясно видимо через рассматривание творений, так что люди не имеют оправдания. —Римлянам 1:18-20. (NIV)

Знание природы укрепляет мою веру в Иисуса. Писание учит, что Бог сотворил всю жизнь за шесть дней, что был всемирный потоп и что животные производят потомство своего рода. По всей земле камни свидетельствуют о всемирном потопе. Люди обнаружили миллиарды окаменелостей — главным образом морских животных — в слоях горных пород, отложенных водой. И животные живут так, как учит Библия о родах. Мы можем наблюдать, как животные повсюду вокруг нас меняются. Меняются их размеры, окраска и пищевые привычки. Рыбы в пещерах утрачивают способность видеть. Клювы птиц приспосабливаются к окружающей среде. При всех этих сложных изменениях все животные остаются в библейских рамках своего рода. Акулы остаются акулами; лягушки остаются лягушками; игуаны остаются игуанами; гиббоны остаются гиббонами. Чем больше я узнаю о природе и наблюдаю за ней, тем больше укрепляется моя вера (уверенность).

В некоторых рассуждениях о вере естественно вспомнить слова Иисуса. После воскресения Иисус является Фоме и говорит ему: …Ты поверил потому, что увидел Меня? Блаженны не видевшие и уверовавшие. —Иоанна 20:29. (ESV) Из этих слов возникает соблазн определить веру как «веру без видения». Но это значит упустить суть. Я не утверждаю, что превосхожу Фому, но он должен был поверить и без того, чтобы увидеть Иисуса. Все свидетельства указывали на это. Во-первых, его добрые друзья, уже доказавшие свою надежность, сказали, что Иисус жив. Во-вторых, Иисус ясно говорил, что воскреснет (см. Матфея 16:21). В-третьих, Иисус уже доказал, что Он Бог, Своей способностью воскрешать мертвых, повелевать погодой, исцелять больных и умножать пищу. У Фомы было все необходимое, чтобы поверить, что Иисус воскрес из мертвых. И все же он пошел против всех доводов и сказал, что ему нужны дополнительные доказательства.

Встретившись с воскресшим Христом, Фома раскаялся в своем неверии и последовал за Христом до самой мученической смерти. К сожалению, дух неверия перед лицом свидетельств и сегодня не исчез из нашего мира. Атеисты, вопреки всем свидетельствам, утверждают, что жизнь может возникнуть из ничего. Они без всяких доказательств заявляют, что рыбы превратились в лягушек. Они слепо цепляются за различные теории, например теорию Большого взрыва, прерывистого равновесия и происхождения с изменениями. У них нет НИКАКИХ убедительных доказательств, но они по-прежнему утверждают, будто основывают все свои мысли на наблюдаемой и воспроизводимой реальности. Христиане, которые из добрых побуждений говорят им, что вера начинается там, где заканчивается разум, невольно играют им на руку. Этому миру не нужно определение веры из социальных сетей. Люди должны увидеть, чем вера является на самом деле: уверенностью в живом Боге, прочно основанной на разуме.

Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it –Matthew 7:13-14.

Of all the word pictures painted by our Lord, it seems this one remains, for the most part, unexplored. On numerous occasions the disciples asked their Master to explain the parables he taught. The parable of the Wheat and Tares resulted in a detailed explanation that leaves little doubt to His intent. …He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man; The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels –Matthew 13:37-39. But in the picture presented as the strait gate, we receive few defining details and are even told that there be but few that will even find it.

The parable is followed by some intense teaching against false prophets, corrupt fruit, and empty words. Some souls will have a pretense of powerful prophecy while missing the gate. Others put forth a front of fruitful freedom but are foreigners to the strait gate. All professing words of goodness, grace, and godliness avail us nothing to the entrance into this gate. Those tramping through the broad gate are obviously more than just the world’s gross, hardened sinners. Rather, the two gates seem to be representative of those who have entered a religious pursuit of life.

Straight and Narrow, as ascribed by the early American revival movement, generally meant “a life of abstinence” from the vices of sin. This is certainly not an entirely wrong perception, yet it seems to differ from the profession of the broad group that had prophesied in thy name? And in thy name have cast out devils? And in thy name done many wonderful works? –Matthew 7:22. To free ourselves from the dregs of evil is quite indispensable to any good living, but he that would enter the strait gate will be he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. –Matthew 7:21. Also, to place asceticism, the doctrine that a person can attain a high spiritual and moral state by practicing self-denial, self-mortification, and the like. –dictionary.com, at the portal of the post seems to invite a works-based, monastic kingdom. Self-denial sings in perfect harmony with the Christian life but will never be found as the sole melody. The ordinances of this world, such as …Touch not; taste not; handle not [are] … after the commandments and doctrines of men. –Colossians 2:20-22. While we applaud the efforts of anyone who has denied himself of this world’s ease and enjoyment for the betterment of others, we cannot offer it as the prescription of the strait gate to the abundant life.

Some will attest that the gate is “Jesus” and all who will enter the kingdom must enter through Him. This certainly carries some merit, as well. In another parable, Christ described Himself as the door of the sheep –John 10:7. Who would care to deny Christ of such a preeminent position? Yet, we have noticed that the “Jesus only” movement has opened the gate so broadly that it can hardly be considered “strait”.

Regardless of our interpretation of what the gate may represent, the decided emphasis given here is upon the adjectives, straight and narrow, as opposed to wide and broad. Strait (Sten-os’) means narrow (from obstacles standing close about) –Strongs. Narrow (Thlee’-bo) means to crowd (literally or figuratively): afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble –Strongs. Here we find some solid definition to our entrance. We must endure an uncomfortable squeeze between two posts if we are to find life. Here we can behold the testimonies of those who have entered there.

  • …we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; (Thlee’-bo) –1 Thessalonians 3:4.
  • …they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted (Thlee’-bo), tormented –Hebrews 11:37.
  • We are troubled (Thlee’-bo) on every side, yet not distressed… –2 Corinthians 4:8.

Herein is an entrance beyond the discipline being taught by the scribes. …when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes –Matthew 7:28-29. The strait gate of Christ rested in a principle beyond word-worn profession. But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished! –Luke 12:50. This is where Christ got His authority: tenaciously doing the will of His Father in heaven by submitting Himself into the hands of men.

One Thing Needful

…The scribes came upon him with the elders, And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority? And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not? But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet. And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was. And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things –Luke 20:1-8.

If the scribes, priests, and elders could have answered this one question they could have understood the power source of His authority. There is an authority of heaven and an authority of men. These two make up the posts of a very strait gate. At times they may even conflict, leaving the conscientious Christian feeling stuck between a rock and a hard place. When earthly authorities overstep their bounds leaving no room to serve God in a Biblical manner, we must choose …to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29. It is here that we will experience the thlee’-bo of the gate.

There is a God-given authority vested in men by their position: government authorities, workplace authorities, parental authorities, and church authorities, to name a few. Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation –Romans 13:1-2. This is strong language that we dare not ignore. Yet the disciples answered such authorities …and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard –Acts 4:19-20. While the disciples carried no personal angst against the rulers, there was a narrow way that they were walking in. Narrow, not because they served God alone, but because they had duel posts to submit to. Patriotism wants to serve man to the exclusion of God. Modern Christianity wants to serve God to the exclusion of man. Both paths are broad, for in either case, we move the opposite post to a position that is less hurtful to our humanity and more pleasing to our palate.

Submission Activates Power.

The authority ushered in by Christ Jesus left His followers astonished and amazed—But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:8. Their experience with authority was a mere social, hierarchical subordination that left them oppressed, pushed down, and forced into subservience. Christ exemplified a new and narrow way. It was not a casting away of civil authority but an empowerment of it. It was a strait gate that respected the authorities enough to volunteer to transport a soldier’s pack the second mile. Today, it is an inner authority that empowers us to respond respectfully and to glorify God while doing it. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13:5. To embrace our authorities in our heart is ultimately the inner channel to freedom and a deterrent to legalism, for it takes to task the issue of sin, sulking, and selfishness, while replacing it with righteousness, well-being, and peace. While many disdain these earthly authorities and remove them as far as possible from their hearts’ compliance, they only succeed to broaden the posts and thus forfeit the life that the strait gate brings. There are a mere few who will find the blessedness within the posts.

These will find life within the confinements of the strait and narrow provided by God and…

…Governments

The humble request of the centurion of Capernaum made Jesus marvel—…Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. He was a man with authority… and under authority. He seemed to understand the correlation in subjection to earthly authority and the exercising of it, for he entreated Christ not to come under his roof but to …speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed –Matthew 8:8. The gate formed by his overseers and the sincere love of his servants under him often left but little room for personal preferences. Yet, the power entwined in his speech was such that the Son of God readily complied with his request!

Joseph repeatedly found himself in tight places between God and the people he served. This resulted in being raised to the second ruling power in the most prominent nation on the earth. Esther and Daniel experienced similar plights. At times, the posts were so narrow that they wondered if they might perish, but the end result was always power… power to live in holiness, power to respond in righteousness, power to overcome victoriously, and power to endure faithfully unto the end.

…Masters

While slavery has been predominantly eradicated in our modern world, the relationship to a master still exists. Employers exercise authority over their servants and greater responsibility is ultimately given to those who submit wholeheartedly to it. The authority given to Eleazer is amazing and inspiring. Abraham trusted him to secure a wife for Isaac; He was even permitted to determine the rules. This colossal commitment left the indentured servant in a tight squeeze between the Master God and his master Abraham. And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham s–Genesis 24:12.

The American workforce has grown very accustomed to refusing anything they esteem as an unreasonable mandate from their employers. In faithless defiance they readily strike and kick the posts further apart to their broad preferences. This attitude has left them spiritually anemic and powerless. The Ethiopian eunuch served God while also serving under Queen Candace. Though his world was narrowed beyond what most of us could ever imagine, …he went on his way rejoicing –Acts 8:39, His life stands as a stellar testimony to Isaiah’s prophecy …neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree –Isaiah 56:3.

…Parents

Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth –Ephesians 6:1-3. This one should be obvious to any spiritually awakened individual. Children, who have parents, have an evident advantage in life and those who respect them, fare even better. Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live? –Hebrews 12:9. Life is found by those who can embrace their earthly fathers and the “Father of spirits”. Those who claim God as their Father while viewing their parents as a mere obstruction to the path they wish to walk in, will sooner or later be walking through the broad gate to destruction.

…Husbands

As Jesus entered into dialogue with the Samaritan woman at Jacob’s well, he began to describe a life that she desperately wanted—… Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come hither to draw. Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither –John 4:16. Christ was seeking to convince her that the abundant life will be found between the two posts. She had previously had five husbands and undoubtedly had not found contentment with any of them. Women who stand up for their rights kick at the narrowness of the gate and forfeit their God-ordained dignity. A woman at rest within the confines of her authorities is not oppressed but is actually liberated and empowered. For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head… –1 Corinthians 11:10. The headship veiling is not just a symbol of submission, nor is it merely a form of protection, it is spiritual power. Her wholehearted subjection fuels a dynamic marriage as she embraces her husband as “lord”, and in doing so, she becomes a faithful vessel of liberty, power, strength, and delegated influence.

…Church Leaders

These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee –Titus 2:15. Many self-proclaimed believers reject any outward display of authority in the Church. To the western mind, church authority is negatively associated with legalism, communism, bondage, and heaviness. But just as a disregard for spiritual authorities stripped Saul of his kingship, so likewise this attitude robs the believer of true authoritative power and nobility. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry… –1 Samuel 15:23. Efforts to choose …a way which seemeth right unto a man… –Proverbs 14:12, leads to bondage, but choosing to walk in surrender and subjection leads to liberation and life. Satan promised Jesus the entire world if He would only throw off the “yoke” of obedience to God. Instead, He set His face like a flint, endured the constraint of subordination, and ultimately liberated the entire world.

Subjection Produces Spiritual Authority

God’s authority and earthly authorities are rooted within the opposing posts of the strait gate. Those fully subject unto them both experience a living authority found within the gate. It brings power unto people rather than power over people. It produces liberty in Christ… the right to the tree of life… freedom from fear… health to our bones… power over unclean spirits… grace to train children… strength to preach and convert souls… and it is the ultimate deterrent to legalism. Faith that comes through wholehearted and humble subjection is the most suspect and under-estimated power available to mankind. Few there be that find it. Why? Because it is fastidiously founded and formulated between the posts of the strait gate and the narrow way.

좁은 문으로 들어가라. 멸망으로 인도하는 문은 크고 그 길이 넓어 그리로 들어가는 자가 많고, 생명으로 인도하는 문은 좁고 그 길이 협착하여 찾는 자가 적음이라 –마태복음 7:13-14.

O우리 주님께서 그리신 여러 비유적 그림 가운데, 이 그림은 대부분 여전히 탐구되지 않은 채로 남아 있는 듯합니다. 제자들은 여러 차례 주님께서 가르치신 비유를 설명해 달라고 요청했습니다. 밀과 가라지의 비유에 대해서는 그분의 의도를 조금도 의심할 여지가 없도록 상세한 설명이 주어졌습니다. …좋은 씨를 뿌리는 이는 인자요 밭은 세상이요 좋은 씨는 천국의 아들들이요 가라지는 악한 자의 아들들이요 가라지를 뿌린 원수는 마귀요 추수 때는 세상 끝이요 추수꾼은 천사들이니라 –마태복음 13:37-39. 그러나 좁은 문으로 제시된 그림에서는 구체적인 설명을 거의 얻지 못하며, 그 문을 찾는 자가 적으리라는 말씀까지 듣습니다.

이 비유 뒤에는 거짓 선지자와 썩은 열매와 헛된 말에 대한 강도 높은 가르침이 이어집니다. 어떤 영혼들은 능력 있는 예언을 하는 체하면서도 그 문을 놓칠 것입니다. 다른 이들은 열매 맺는 자유를 내세우지만 좁은 문과는 무관한 이들입니다. 선함과 은혜와 경건을 말로 고백한다고 해서 이 문으로 들어가는 데 아무런 유익도 얻지 못합니다. 넓은 문으로 몰려드는 이들은 세상의 극악하고 완악한 죄인들에 불과한 것이 분명 아닙니다. 오히려 두 문은 종교적 삶을 추구하는 길에 들어선 이들을 나타내는 듯합니다.

좁고 곧은 길(Straight and Narrow), 초기 미국 부흥 운동에서 사용된 이 표현은 일반적으로 죄의 악습을 “삼가는 삶”을 뜻했습니다. 이것이 전적으로 잘못된 인식은 분명 아니지만, 넓은 무리의 고백과는 다른 듯합니다. 그들은 주의 이름으로 예언하지 아니하였나이까? 주의 이름으로 귀신을 쫓아내지 아니하였나이까? 주의 이름으로 많은 권능을 행하지 아니하였나이까? –마태복음 7:22. 악의 찌꺼기에서 벗어나는 것은 선한 삶을 위해 꼭 필요하지만, 좁은 문으로 들어가려는 자는 하늘에 계신 내 아버지의 뜻을 행하는 자라야 하리라. –마태복음 7:21. 또한 금욕주의, 곧 사람이 자기 부인과 자기 고행 등을 실천함으로써 높은 영적·도덕적 상태에 이를 수 있다는 교리. –dictionary.com를 문 앞에 두는 것은 행위에 기초한 수도원적 왕국을 연상시키기 쉽습니다. 자기 부인은 그리스도인의 삶과 완벽한 조화를 이루지만, 결코 그것만이 유일한 선율인 것은 아닙니다. …붙잡지도 말고 맛보지도 말고 만지지도 말라[는 규례들은] … 사람의 계명과 교훈을 따르는 것이라. –골로새서 2:20-22. 다른 이들의 유익을 위해 세상의 안락과 즐거움을 마다한 이들의 노력을 우리는 칭찬하지만, 그것을 풍성한 생명에 이르는 좁은 문을 위한 처방으로 제시할 수는 없습니다.

어떤 이들은 그 문이 “예수님”이며, 천국에 들어갈 모든 사람은 그분을 통해 들어가야 한다고 말할 것입니다. 이 주장에도 분명 일리가 있습니다. 다른 비유에서 그리스도께서는 자신을 양의 문 –요한복음 10:7.이라고 묘사하셨습니다. 누가 그리스도의 그러한 탁월한 지위를 부인하려 하겠습니까? 그러나 우리는 “오직 예수” 운동이 문을 너무 넓게 열어 두어 더는 “좁다”고 보기 어려울 만큼 만들었다는 점을 알아차렸습니다.

문이 무엇을 나타내는지 우리가 어떻게 해석하든, 여기서 강조되는 것은 좁고 협착함이지 크고 넓음이 아닙니다. 좁은(Strait) (스테노스)은 가까이 둘러선 장애물들 때문에 좁은 –스트롱 사전.을 뜻합니다. 협착한(Narrow) (틀리보)은 붐비게 하다(문자적으로나 비유적으로): 괴롭히다, 좁히다, 몰려들다, 환난을 겪다, 곤란하게 하다 –스트롱 사전.를 뜻합니다. 여기서 우리는 들어가는 길에 대한 확실한 정의를 찾습니다. 생명을 얻으려면 두 기둥 사이에서 불편하게 몸을 죄는 일을 견뎌야 합니다. 여기서 우리는 그곳으로 들어간 이들의 증언을 볼 수 있습니다.

  • …우리가 환난을 당할 것을 너희에게 미리 말하였더니(틀리보) –데살로니가전서 3:4.
  • …양과 염소의 가죽을 입고 유리하여 궁핍하며 환난을 당하며(틀리보) 괴로움을 받았으니 –히브리서 11:37.
  • 우리가 사방으로 환난을 당하여도(틀리보) 눌리지 아니하며… –고린도후서 4:8.

여기에는 서기관들이 가르친 훈육을 넘어서는 들어감이 있습니다. …예수께서 이 말씀을 마치시매 무리들이 그 가르치심에 놀라니 이는 그 가르치시는 것이 권위 있는 자와 같고 그들의 서기관들과 같지 아니함일러라 –마태복음 7:28-29. 그리스도의 좁은 문은 말뿐인 진부한 고백을 넘어서는 원리에 기초했습니다. 내가 받을 세례가 있으니 그 일이 이루어질 때까지 내가 얼마나 답답하겠느냐! –누가복음 12:50. 그리스도께서 권위를 얻으신 것은 바로 이 길을 통해서였습니다. 하늘에 계신 아버지의 뜻을 굳건히 행하시며 자신을 사람들의 손에 내어 주신 것입니다.

필요한 한 가지

…서기관들이 장로들과 함께 와서 예수께 말하되, 당신이 무슨 권위로 이런 일을 하느냐? 누가 이런 권위를 주었느냐? 예수께서 대답하여 이르시되 나도 한 가지를 너희에게 물으리니 내게 대답하라. 요한의 세례가 하늘로부터냐 사람으로부터냐? 그들이 서로 의논하여 이르되 하늘로부터라 하면 어찌하여 그를 믿지 아니하였느냐 할 것이요, 사람으로부터라 하면 모든 백성이 우리를 돌로 치리니 이는 그들이 요한을 선지자로 확신함이로다 하고, 그들이 어디로부터인지 알지 못한다고 대답하니 예수께서 그들에게 이르시되 나도 무슨 권위로 이런 일을 하는지 너희에게 이르지 아니하리라 하시니라 –누가복음 20:1-8.

서기관과 제사장과 장로들이 이 한 가지 질문에 답할 수 있었다면, 그들은 그분의 권위가 어디에서 오는지 이해할 수 있었을 것입니다. 하늘의 권위와 사람의 권위가 있습니다. 이 두 권위가 매우 좁은 문의 두 기둥을 이룹니다. 때로는 서로 충돌하기도 하여, 양심적인 그리스도인이 진퇴양난에 빠진 듯 느끼게 합니다. 세상의 권위가 한계를 넘어 성경적인 방식으로 하나님을 섬길 여지를 남기지 않을 때, 우리는 …사람보다 하나님께 순종하는 것이 마땅하니라 –사도행전 5:29.를 택해야 합니다. 바로 여기서 우리는 문의 틀리보를 경험하게 됩니다.

하나님께서 직분에 따라 사람들에게 맡기신 권위가 있습니다. 예를 들면 정부의 권위, 직장의 권위, 부모의 권위, 교회 지도자의 권위입니다. 각 사람은 위에 있는 권세들에게 복종하라. 권세는 하나님으로부터 나지 않음이 없나니, 있는 권세들은 하나님께서 정하신 바라. 그러므로 권세를 거스르는 자는 하나님의 명을 거스름이니 거스르는 자들은 심판을 자초하리라 –로마서 13:1-2. 이는 감히 무시할 수 없는 강한 표현입니다. 그러나 제자들은 그러한 권위자들에게 …이르되 하나님 앞에서 너희 말을 듣는 것이 하나님의 말씀을 듣는 것보다 옳은가 판단하라. 우리는 보고 들은 것을 말하지 아니할 수 없다 하니 –사도행전 4:19-20.라고 대답했습니다. 제자들은 다스리는 자들에게 사적인 반감을 품지 않았지만, 그들이 걸어가는 길은 좁았습니다. 그들이 하나님만 섬겼기 때문이 아니라, 복종해야 할 기둥이 둘이었기 때문에 좁았던 것입니다. 애국주의는 하나님을 제외하고 사람을 섬기려 합니다. 현대 기독교는 사람을 제외하고 하나님을 섬기려 합니다. 어느 쪽이든 인간적으로 덜 고통스럽고 입맛에 더 맞는 자리로 반대편 기둥을 옮기므로, 두 길 모두 넓습니다.

복종은 능력을 활성화합니다.

그리스도 예수께서 열어 보이신 권위에 그분을 따르는 이들은 놀라고 경탄했습니다. 무리가 보고 두려워하며 이런 권능을 사람에게 주신 하나님께 영광을 돌리니라 –마태복음 9:8. 그들이 경험한 권위란 억압받고 짓눌리며 강제로 복종하게 만드는, 그저 사회적·계층적 종속에 불과했습니다. 그리스도께서는 새롭고 좁은 길을 보여 주셨습니다. 그것은 시민 권위를 내던지는 일이 아니라 그 권위에 힘을 실어 주는 일이었습니다. 병사의 짐을 자원하여 두 번째 길까지 져다 줄 만큼 권위를 존중하는 좁은 문이었습니다. 오늘날 그것은 우리가 존중하는 태도로 반응하고, 그렇게 하면서 하나님께 영광을 돌리도록 힘을 주는 내면의 권위입니다. 그러므로 노여움을 피하기 위하여만 복종할 것이 아니요 양심을 위하여도 할 것이라 –로마서 13:5. 마음으로 권위에 순복하는 것은 궁극적으로 자유에 이르는 내면의 통로이며 율법주의를 막아 줍니다. 죄와 불만과 이기심의 문제를 다루고, 그 자리에 의와 안녕과 평화를 대신 놓기 때문입니다. 많은 이들이 세상의 권위를 멸시하고 마음의 순종에서 가능한 한 멀리 밀어내지만, 그들은 기둥 사이를 넓히는 데 성공할 뿐이며, 그리하여 좁은 문이 가져다주는 생명을 잃습니다. 그 기둥 사이에 있는 복됨을 발견할 이는 극히 적습니다.

이들은 하나님께서 마련하신 좁고 협착한 경계 안에서 생명을 찾을 것이며…

…정부

가버나움 백부장의 겸손한 요청에 예수께서는 놀라셨습니다. …내가 진실로 너희에게 이르노니 이스라엘 중 아무에게서도 이만한 믿음을 보지 못하였노라 –마태복음 8:10. 그는 권세 아래 있으면서 권세를 가진 사람이었습니다. 그는 세상의 권위에 복종하는 것과 권위를 행사하는 것 사이의 연관성을 이해한 듯했습니다. 그리스도께 자기 집에 오시지 말고 …말씀만 하옵소서 그러면 내 하인이 낫겠나이다 –마태복음 8:8.라고 청했기 때문입니다. 그의 윗사람들이 세운 문과 그가 거느린 종들에 대한 진실한 사랑 사이에서는 개인적인 선호를 내세울 여지가 거의 없었을 것입니다. 그러나 그의 말에 얽힌 능력은 하나님의 아들께서 기꺼이 그의 요청을 들어주실 정도였습니다!

요셉은 하나님과 자신이 섬기는 사람들 사이에서 곤란한 처지에 놓이는 일이 거듭되었습니다. 그 결과 그는 지상에서 가장 강대한 나라에서 통치권을 가진 제2인자의 지위에 올랐습니다. 에스더와 다니엘도 비슷한 곤경을 겪었습니다. 때로는 기둥 사이가 너무 좁아 죽을지도 모른다고 여겼지만, 그 끝에는 언제나 능력이 있었습니다. 거룩하게 살 능력, 의롭게 반응할 능력, 승리로 이겨 낼 능력, 그리고 끝까지 신실하게 견딜 능력이었습니다.

…주인

현대 사회에서 노예 제도는 대부분 사라졌지만, 주인과의 관계는 여전히 존재합니다. 고용주는 종들에게 권위를 행사하며, 그 권위에 온 마음으로 복종하는 이들에게는 궁극적으로 더 큰 책임이 주어집니다. 엘리에셀에게 맡겨진 권위는 놀랍고도 고무적입니다. 아브라함은 이삭의 아내를 구하는 일을 그에게 믿고 맡겼으며, 규칙을 정하는 일까지 허락했습니다. 이처럼 막중한 위임은 종의 신분이던 그를 주 하나님과 주인 아브라함 사이의 좁은 틈에 놓았습니다. 그가 이르되 내 주인 아브라함의 하나님 여호와여 원하건대 오늘 나에게 순조로운 길을 열어 주시고 내 주인 아브라함에게 은혜를 베푸소서 –창세기 24:12.

미국의 노동자들은 고용주가 불합리하다고 여기는 요구를 거부하는 데 매우 익숙해졌습니다. 믿음 없는 반항으로 그들은 파업을 하고 기둥을 더 벌려 자신들이 선호하는 넓은 길을 만듭니다. 이러한 태도는 그들을 영적으로 무기력하고 무능하게 만들었습니다. 에티오피아 내시는 하나님을 섬기는 동시에 간다게 여왕을 섬겼습니다. 그의 세상은 우리 대부분이 상상할 수 있는 것보다 훨씬 더 좁아졌지만, …기쁨으로 길을 가더라 –사도행전 8:39. 그의 삶은 이사야의 예언을 탁월하게 증언합니다. …고자도 나는 마른 나무라 말하지 말라 –이사야 56:3.

…부모

자녀들아 주 안에서 너희 부모에게 순종하라 이것이 옳으니라. 네 아버지와 어머니를 공경하라 이것은 약속이 있는 첫 계명이니, 이는 네가 잘되고 땅에서 장수하리라 –에베소서 6:1-3. 영적으로 깨어난 사람이라면 누구나 이 점은 분명히 알 것입니다. 부모가 있는 자녀는 삶에서 분명한 이점을 누리며, 부모를 존중하는 자녀는 더 잘 살아갑니다. 또 우리 육신의 아버지가 우리를 징계하여도 공경하였거든 하물며 영들의 아버지께 더욱 복종하고 살아야 하지 않겠느냐? –히브리서 12:9. 육신의 아버지와 “영들의 아버지”를 함께 받아들일 수 있는 이들이 생명을 얻습니다. 하나님을 아버지라 부르면서도 부모를 자신이 걷고 싶은 길을 막는 장애물에 불과한 것으로 여기는 이들은 머지않아 멸망으로 인도하는 넓은 문으로 들어서게 될 것입니다.

…남편

예수께서는 야곱의 우물가에서 사마리아 여인과 대화를 나누시며, 그 여인이 간절히 원하던 삶을 말씀하기 시작하셨습니다. …주여 그런 물을 내게 주사 목마르지도 않고 또 여기 물 길으러 오지도 않게 하옵소서. 예수께서 이르시되 가서 네 남편을 불러 오라 –요한복음 4:15-16. 그리스도께서는 풍성한 생명이 두 기둥 사이에서 발견된다는 것을 그 여인이 깨닫게 하려 하셨습니다. 그 여인은 앞서 남편이 다섯이나 있었고, 어느 누구와도 만족을 찾지 못했음이 틀림없습니다. 자신의 권리를 주장하는 여성들은 문의 좁음에 맞서고 하나님께서 정하신 존엄을 잃습니다. 권위의 경계 안에서 평안히 거하는 여성은 억압받는 것이 아니라 오히려 자유와 능력을 얻습니다. 이러므로 여자는 천사들로 말미암아 권위 아래 있는 표를 그 머리 위에 둘지니라… –고린도전서 11:10. 머리를 가리는 것은 복종의 상징일 뿐도 아니고 단순한 보호의 수단일 뿐도 아닙니다. 그것은 영적 능력입니다. 여성이 온 마음으로 복종할 때 역동적인 결혼 생활에 힘이 실립니다. 남편을 “주”로 받아들이며, 그리하여 자유와 능력과 힘과 위임받은 영향력을 지닌 신실한 그릇이 됩니다.

…교회 지도자

너는 이것들을 말하고 권면하며 모든 권위로 책망하여 아무도 너를 업신여기지 못하게 하라 –디도서 2:15. 스스로 믿는 자라 칭하는 많은 이들이 교회 안에서 권위가 드러나는 것을 거부합니다. 서구적 사고방식에서 교회의 권위는 율법주의와 공산주의와 속박과 무거움과 부정적으로 연관됩니다. 그러나 영적 권위를 무시한 탓에 사울이 왕위를 잃었듯, 이러한 태도 역시 신자에게서 참된 권위의 능력과 존귀함을 빼앗습니다. 이는 거역하는 것은 점치는 죄와 같고 완고한 것은 사신 우상에게 절하는 죄와 같음이라… –사무엘상 15:23. 사람이 보기에 옳아 보이는 길을 택하려는 노력은… –잠언 14:12, 속박으로 이어지지만, 항복과 복종 가운데 걷기를 택하면 해방과 생명으로 이어집니다. 사탄은 예수께 하나님께 순종하는 “멍에”만 벗어던지면 온 세상을 주겠다고 약속했습니다. 그러나 그분은 얼굴을 부싯돌처럼 굳게 하시고 종속의 제약을 견디셨으며, 마침내 온 세상을 해방하셨습니다.

복종은 영적 권위를 낳습니다

하나님의 권위와 세상의 권위는 좁은 문의 서로 마주 선 두 기둥에 뿌리를 두고 있습니다. 그 두 권위에 온전히 복종하는 이들은 문 안에서 살아 있는 권위를 경험합니다. 그것은 사람들을 지배하는 권력이 아니라 사람들에게 주는 권력을 가져옵니다. 그리스도 안의 자유… 생명나무에 대한 권리… 두려움에서 벗어남… 뼈에 양약이 됨… 더러운 영들을 다스리는 능력… 자녀를 훈육할 은혜… 말씀을 전하고 영혼을 회심시킬 힘을 낳으며… 율법주의를 막는 궁극적인 방패입니다. 온 마음을 다한 겸손한 복종을 통해 오는 믿음은 인류가 누릴 수 있는 능력 가운데 가장 의심받고 과소평가되는 능력입니다. 찾는 이가 적습니다. 왜일까요? 그 능력은 좁은 문의 기둥 사이, 좁은 길 위에 세심하게 기초를 두고 형성되기 때문입니다.

Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it –Matthew 7:13-14.

Of all the word pictures painted by our Lord, it seems this one remains, for the most part, unexplored. On numerous occasions the disciples asked their Master to explain the parables he taught. The parable of the Wheat and Tares resulted in a detailed explanation that leaves little doubt to His intent. …He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man; The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels –Matthew 13:37-39. But in the picture presented as the strait gate, we receive few defining details and are even told that there be but few that will even find it.

The parable is followed by some intense teaching against false prophets, corrupt fruit, and empty words. Some souls will have a pretense of powerful prophecy while missing the gate. Others put forth a front of fruitful freedom but are foreigners to the strait gate. All professing words of goodness, grace, and godliness avail us nothing to the entrance into this gate. Those tramping through the broad gate are obviously more than just the world’s gross, hardened sinners. Rather, the two gates seem to be representative of those who have entered a religious pursuit of life.

Straight and Narrow, as ascribed by the early American revival movement, generally meant “a life of abstinence” from the vices of sin. This is certainly not an entirely wrong perception, yet it seems to differ from the profession of the broad group that had prophesied in thy name? And in thy name have cast out devils? And in thy name done many wonderful works? –Matthew 7:22. To free ourselves from the dregs of evil is quite indispensable to any good living, but he that would enter the strait gate will be he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. –Matthew 7:21. Also, to place asceticism, the doctrine that a person can attain a high spiritual and moral state by practicing self-denial, self-mortification, and the like. –dictionary.com, at the portal of the post seems to invite a works-based, monastic kingdom. Self-denial sings in perfect harmony with the Christian life but will never be found as the sole melody. The ordinances of this world, such as …Touch not; taste not; handle not [are] … after the commandments and doctrines of men. –Colossians 2:20-22. While we applaud the efforts of anyone who has denied himself of this world’s ease and enjoyment for the betterment of others, we cannot offer it as the prescription of the strait gate to the abundant life.

Some will attest that the gate is “Jesus” and all who will enter the kingdom must enter through Him. This certainly carries some merit, as well. In another parable, Christ described Himself as the door of the sheep –John 10:7. Who would care to deny Christ of such a preeminent position? Yet, we have noticed that the “Jesus only” movement has opened the gate so broadly that it can hardly be considered “strait”.

Regardless of our interpretation of what the gate may represent, the decided emphasis given here is upon the adjectives, straight and narrow, as opposed to wide and broad. Strait (Sten-os’) means narrow (from obstacles standing close about) –Strongs. Narrow (Thlee’-bo) means to crowd (literally or figuratively): afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble –Strongs. Here we find some solid definition to our entrance. We must endure an uncomfortable squeeze between two posts if we are to find life. Here we can behold the testimonies of those who have entered there.

  • …we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; (Thlee’-bo) –1 Thessalonians 3:4.
  • …they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted (Thlee’-bo), tormented –Hebrews 11:37.
  • We are troubled (Thlee’-bo) on every side, yet not distressed… –2 Corinthians 4:8.

Herein is an entrance beyond the discipline being taught by the scribes. …when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes –Matthew 7:28-29. The strait gate of Christ rested in a principle beyond word-worn profession. But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished! –Luke 12:50. This is where Christ got His authority: tenaciously doing the will of His Father in heaven by submitting Himself into the hands of men.

One Thing Needful

…The scribes came upon him with the elders, And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority? And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not? But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet. And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was. And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things –Luke 20:1-8.

If the scribes, priests, and elders could have answered this one question they could have understood the power source of His authority. There is an authority of heaven and an authority of men. These two make up the posts of a very strait gate. At times they may even conflict, leaving the conscientious Christian feeling stuck between a rock and a hard place. When earthly authorities overstep their bounds leaving no room to serve God in a Biblical manner, we must choose …to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29. It is here that we will experience the thlee’-bo of the gate.

There is a God-given authority vested in men by their position: government authorities, workplace authorities, parental authorities, and church authorities, to name a few. Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation –Romans 13:1-2. This is strong language that we dare not ignore. Yet the disciples answered such authorities …and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard –Acts 4:19-20. While the disciples carried no personal angst against the rulers, there was a narrow way that they were walking in. Narrow, not because they served God alone, but because they had duel posts to submit to. Patriotism wants to serve man to the exclusion of God. Modern Christianity wants to serve God to the exclusion of man. Both paths are broad, for in either case, we move the opposite post to a position that is less hurtful to our humanity and more pleasing to our palate.

Submission Activates Power.

The authority ushered in by Christ Jesus left His followers astonished and amazed—But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:8. Their experience with authority was a mere social, hierarchical subordination that left them oppressed, pushed down, and forced into subservience. Christ exemplified a new and narrow way. It was not a casting away of civil authority but an empowerment of it. It was a strait gate that respected the authorities enough to volunteer to transport a soldier’s pack the second mile. Today, it is an inner authority that empowers us to respond respectfully and to glorify God while doing it. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13:5. To embrace our authorities in our heart is ultimately the inner channel to freedom and a deterrent to legalism, for it takes to task the issue of sin, sulking, and selfishness, while replacing it with righteousness, well-being, and peace. While many disdain these earthly authorities and remove them as far as possible from their hearts’ compliance, they only succeed to broaden the posts and thus forfeit the life that the strait gate brings. There are a mere few who will find the blessedness within the posts.

These will find life within the confinements of the strait and narrow provided by God and…

…Governments

The humble request of the centurion of Capernaum made Jesus marvel—…Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. He was a man with authority… and under authority. He seemed to understand the correlation in subjection to earthly authority and the exercising of it, for he entreated Christ not to come under his roof but to …speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed –Matthew 8:8. The gate formed by his overseers and the sincere love of his servants under him often left but little room for personal preferences. Yet, the power entwined in his speech was such that the Son of God readily complied with his request!

Joseph repeatedly found himself in tight places between God and the people he served. This resulted in being raised to the second ruling power in the most prominent nation on the earth. Esther and Daniel experienced similar plights. At times, the posts were so narrow that they wondered if they might perish, but the end result was always power… power to live in holiness, power to respond in righteousness, power to overcome victoriously, and power to endure faithfully unto the end.

…Masters

While slavery has been predominantly eradicated in our modern world, the relationship to a master still exists. Employers exercise authority over their servants and greater responsibility is ultimately given to those who submit wholeheartedly to it. The authority given to Eleazer is amazing and inspiring. Abraham trusted him to secure a wife for Isaac; He was even permitted to determine the rules. This colossal commitment left the indentured servant in a tight squeeze between the Master God and his master Abraham. And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham s–Genesis 24:12.

The American workforce has grown very accustomed to refusing anything they esteem as an unreasonable mandate from their employers. In faithless defiance they readily strike and kick the posts further apart to their broad preferences. This attitude has left them spiritually anemic and powerless. The Ethiopian eunuch served God while also serving under Queen Candace. Though his world was narrowed beyond what most of us could ever imagine, …he went on his way rejoicing –Acts 8:39, His life stands as a stellar testimony to Isaiah’s prophecy …neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree –Isaiah 56:3.

…Parents

Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth –Ephesians 6:1-3. This one should be obvious to any spiritually awakened individual. Children, who have parents, have an evident advantage in life and those who respect them, fare even better. Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live? –Hebrews 12:9. Life is found by those who can embrace their earthly fathers and the “Father of spirits”. Those who claim God as their Father while viewing their parents as a mere obstruction to the path they wish to walk in, will sooner or later be walking through the broad gate to destruction.

…Husbands

As Jesus entered into dialogue with the Samaritan woman at Jacob’s well, he began to describe a life that she desperately wanted—… Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come hither to draw. Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither –John 4:16. Christ was seeking to convince her that the abundant life will be found between the two posts. She had previously had five husbands and undoubtedly had not found contentment with any of them. Women who stand up for their rights kick at the narrowness of the gate and forfeit their God-ordained dignity. A woman at rest within the confines of her authorities is not oppressed but is actually liberated and empowered. For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head… –1 Corinthians 11:10. The headship veiling is not just a symbol of submission, nor is it merely a form of protection, it is spiritual power. Her wholehearted subjection fuels a dynamic marriage as she embraces her husband as “lord”, and in doing so, she becomes a faithful vessel of liberty, power, strength, and delegated influence.

…Church Leaders

These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee –Titus 2:15. Many self-proclaimed believers reject any outward display of authority in the Church. To the western mind, church authority is negatively associated with legalism, communism, bondage, and heaviness. But just as a disregard for spiritual authorities stripped Saul of his kingship, so likewise this attitude robs the believer of true authoritative power and nobility. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry… –1 Samuel 15:23. Efforts to choose …a way which seemeth right unto a man… –Proverbs 14:12, leads to bondage, but choosing to walk in surrender and subjection leads to liberation and life. Satan promised Jesus the entire world if He would only throw off the “yoke” of obedience to God. Instead, He set His face like a flint, endured the constraint of subordination, and ultimately liberated the entire world.

Subjection Produces Spiritual Authority

God’s authority and earthly authorities are rooted within the opposing posts of the strait gate. Those fully subject unto them both experience a living authority found within the gate. It brings power unto people rather than power over people. It produces liberty in Christ… the right to the tree of life… freedom from fear… health to our bones… power over unclean spirits… grace to train children… strength to preach and convert souls… and it is the ultimate deterrent to legalism. Faith that comes through wholehearted and humble subjection is the most suspect and under-estimated power available to mankind. Few there be that find it. Why? Because it is fastidiously founded and formulated between the posts of the strait gate and the narrow way.

Geht hinein durch das enge Tor; denn weit ist das Tor und breit der Weg, der ins Verderben führt, und viele sind es, die durch dieses Tor hineingehen. Denn eng ist das Tor und schmal der Weg, der zum Leben führt, und wenige sind es, die ihn finden –Matthäus 7:13-14.

Von all den Wortbildern, die unser Herr gemalt hat, scheint dieses größtenteils unerforscht geblieben zu sein. Bei zahlreichen Gelegenheiten baten die Jünger ihren Meister, die Gleichnisse zu erklären, die er lehrte. Das Gleichnis vom Weizen und Unkraut führte zu einer ausführlichen Erklärung, die kaum Zweifel an seiner Absicht lässt. …Der den guten Samen sät, ist der Sohn des Menschen; das Feld ist die Welt; der gute Same sind die Kinder des Reiches; das Unkraut aber sind die Kinder des Bösen. Der Feind, der es gesät hat, ist der Teufel; die Ernte ist das Ende der Welt, und die Schnitter sind die Engel –Matthäus 13:37-39. Doch bei dem Bild vom engen Tor erhalten wir nur wenige erklärende Einzelheiten, und es wird uns sogar gesagt, dass es nur wenige geben wird, die es überhaupt finden.

Auf das Gleichnis folgt eine eindringliche Lehre gegen falsche Propheten, verdorbene Frucht und leere Worte. Manche Seelen werden den Anschein machtvoller Prophetie erwecken und doch das Tor verfehlen. Andere geben sich den Anschein fruchtbarer Freiheit, sind dem engen Tor aber fremd. Alle Bekenntnisse von Güte, Gnade und Frömmigkeit nützen uns beim Eintritt durch dieses Tor nichts. Diejenigen, die durch das breite Tor trampeln, sind offensichtlich nicht nur die groben, verhärteten Sünder der Welt. Vielmehr scheinen die beiden Tore für diejenigen zu stehen, die sich auf eine religiöse Lebensausrichtung eingelassen haben.

Der gerade und schmale Weg, wie ihn die frühe amerikanische Erweckungsbewegung bezeichnete, bedeutete gewöhnlich „ein Leben der Enthaltsamkeit“ von den Lastern der Sünde. Das ist gewiss nicht völlig falsch verstanden, doch scheint es sich von dem Bekenntnis der breiten Gruppe zu unterscheiden, die in deinem Namen geweissagt? Und in deinem Namen Dämonen ausgetrieben? Und in deinem Namen viele Wunder getan? –Matthäus 7:22. Sich von den Niederungen des Bösen zu befreien, ist für ein gutes Leben durchaus unerlässlich; doch wer durch das enge Tor eintreten will, muss den Willen meines Vaters tun, der im Himmel ist. –Matthäus 7:21. Auch scheint es, Askese –die Lehre, dass ein Mensch durch Selbstverleugnung, Selbstkasteiung und Ähnliches einen hohen geistlichen und moralischen Zustand erreichen kann. –dictionary.com– an den Eingang des Pfostens zu setzen, ein auf Werkgerechtigkeit beruhendes, klösterliches Reich nahezulegen. Selbstverleugnung klingt vollkommen harmonisch mit dem christlichen Leben, wird aber niemals die einzige Melodie sein. Die Satzungen dieser Welt, wie …Rühre nicht an, koste nicht, betaste nicht [sind] … nach den Geboten und Lehren von Menschen. –Kolosser 2:20-22. Wir begrüßen zwar die Bemühungen jedes Menschen, der sich den Komfort und Genuss dieser Welt zum Wohl anderer versagt hat, können dies aber nicht als das Rezept für das enge Tor zum Leben in Fülle anbieten.

Manche werden behaupten, das Tor sei „Jesus“ und alle, die in das Reich eingehen, müssten durch ihn eintreten. Auch daran ist gewiss etwas Wahres. In einem anderen Gleichnis beschrieb Christus sich selbst als die Tür der Schafe –Johannes 10:7. Wer würde Christus eine derart herausragende Stellung absprechen wollen? Doch haben wir bemerkt, dass die Bewegung „Jesus allein“ das Tor so weit geöffnet hat, dass es kaum noch als „eng“ gelten kann.

Unabhängig davon, wie wir deuten, wofür das Tor stehen mag, liegt die deutliche Betonung hier auf den Adjektiven gerade und schmal, im Gegensatz zu weit und breit. Eng (Sten-os’) bedeutet schmal (durch Hindernisse, die dicht ringsum stehen) –Strongs. Schmal (Thlee’-bo) bedeutet drängen (wörtlich oder bildlich): bedrängen, einengen, bedrängen, Trübsal erleiden, in Not sein –Strongs. Hier finden wir eine klare Bestimmung für unseren Eingang. Wenn wir das Leben finden wollen, müssen wir die unangenehme Enge zwischen zwei Pfosten ertragen. Hier können wir die Zeugnisse derer betrachten, die dort eingetreten sind.

  • …wir haben euch vorhergesagt, dass wir Trübsal erleiden würden; (Thlee’-bo) –1. Thessalonicher 3:4.
  • …sie zogen umher in Schaf- und Ziegenfellen; mittellos, bedrängt (Thlee’-bo), gequält –Hebräer 11:37.
  • Wir sind von allen Seiten bedrängt (Thlee’-bo), aber nicht eingeengt… –2. Korinther 4:8.

Hierin liegt ein Eingang, der über die von den Schriftgelehrten gelehrte Disziplin hinausgeht. …Als Jesus diese Worte beendet hatte, erstaunte die Volksmenge über seine Lehre; denn er lehrte sie wie einer, der Vollmacht hat, und nicht wie ihre Schriftgelehrten –Matthäus 7:28-29. Das enge Tor Christi gründete auf einem Prinzip, das über abgedroschene Bekenntnisse hinausging. Aber ich muss mit einer Taufe getauft werden, und wie bin ich bedrängt, bis sie vollbracht ist! –Lukas 12:50. Hierher rührte Christi Vollmacht: Er tat beharrlich den Willen seines Vaters im Himmel und gab sich in die Hände der Menschen.

Eines ist nötig

…Die Schriftgelehrten kamen mit den Ältesten zu ihm und sagten: Sag uns, mit welcher Vollmacht tust du dies? Oder wer hat dir diese Vollmacht gegeben? Er aber antwortete und sagte zu ihnen: Auch ich will euch eine Frage stellen; antwortet mir: War die Taufe des Johannes vom Himmel oder von Menschen? Da überlegten sie untereinander und sagten: Wenn wir sagen: Vom Himmel, wird er sagen: Warum habt ihr ihm dann nicht geglaubt? Wenn wir aber sagen: Von Menschen, wird uns das ganze Volk steinigen; denn sie sind überzeugt, dass Johannes ein Prophet war. Und sie antworteten, sie wüssten nicht, woher sie war. Jesus sagte zu ihnen: Dann sage auch ich euch nicht, mit welcher Vollmacht ich dies tue –Lukas 20:1-8.

Hätten die Schriftgelehrten, Priester und Ältesten diese eine Frage beantworten können, hätten sie die Quelle der Macht seiner Vollmacht verstanden. Es gibt eine Vollmacht des Himmels und eine Vollmacht der Menschen. Diese beiden bilden die Pfosten eines sehr engen Tores. Manchmal können sie sogar miteinander in Konflikt geraten, sodass sich der gewissenhafte Christ zwischen Hammer und Amboss fühlt. Wenn irdische Autoritäten ihre Grenzen überschreiten und keinen Raum lassen, Gott auf biblische Weise zu dienen, müssen wir wählen, …Gott mehr zu gehorchen als den Menschen –Apostelgeschichte 5:29. Hier werden wir die Thlee’-bo-Enge des Tores erfahren.

Es gibt eine von Gott verliehene Autorität, die Menschen aufgrund ihrer Stellung innehaben: staatliche Autoritäten, Vorgesetzte am Arbeitsplatz, Eltern und kirchliche Leiter, um nur einige zu nennen. Jede Seele sei den übergeordneten Gewalten untertan. Denn es gibt keine Gewalt außer von Gott; die bestehenden Gewalten sind von Gott eingesetzt. Wer sich daher der Gewalt widersetzt, widersetzt sich der Anordnung Gottes; die sich aber widersetzen, werden sich selbst das Gericht zuziehen –Römer 13:1-2. Das sind starke Worte, die wir nicht wagen dürfen zu übergehen. Doch antworteten die Jünger solchen Autoritäten: …und sagten zu ihnen: Ob es vor Gott recht ist, euch mehr zu gehorchen als Gott, das beurteilt ihr. Denn wir können nicht anders, als von dem zu reden, was wir gesehen und gehört haben –Apostelgeschichte 4:19-20. Die Jünger hegten keinen persönlichen Groll gegen die Herrscher, doch sie gingen einen schmalen Weg. Schmal war er nicht deshalb, weil sie allein Gott dienten, sondern weil sie sich zwei Pfosten unterordnen mussten. Patriotismus will dem Menschen unter Ausschluss Gottes dienen. Modernes Christentum will Gott unter Ausschluss des Menschen dienen. Beide Wege sind breit, denn in beiden Fällen verschieben wir den gegenüberliegenden Pfosten an eine Stelle, die unserer Menschlichkeit weniger wehtut und unserem Geschmack besser gefällt.

Unterordnung setzt Kraft frei.

Die durch Christus Jesus eingeführte Vollmacht ließ seine Nachfolger erstaunt und verwundert zurück –Als aber die Volksmengen es sahen, verwunderten sie sich und verherrlichten Gott, der den Menschen solche Vollmacht gegeben hatte –Matthäus 9:8. Ihre Erfahrung mit Autorität bestand lediglich in einer sozialen, hierarchischen Unterordnung, durch die sie unterdrückt, herabgedrückt und zur Unterwürfigkeit gezwungen wurden. Christus zeigte einen neuen und schmalen Weg. Es war keine Verwerfung staatlicher Autorität, sondern eine Stärkung derselben. Es war ein enges Tor, das die Autoritäten so weit respektierte, dass man sich freiwillig bereit erklärte, das Gepäck eines Soldaten eine zweite Meile zu tragen. Heute ist es eine innere Vollmacht, die uns befähigt, respektvoll zu reagieren und dabei Gott zu verherrlichen. Darum müsst ihr euch unterordnen, nicht nur um des Zorns willen, sondern auch um des Gewissens willen –Römer 13:5. Unsere Autoritäten in unser Herz aufzunehmen, ist letztlich der innere Weg zur Freiheit und ein Hindernis für Gesetzlichkeit, denn so nehmen wir uns der Sünde, des Schmollens und der Selbstsucht an und ersetzen sie durch Gerechtigkeit, Wohlergehen und Frieden. Viele verachten diese irdischen Autoritäten und halten sie so weit wie möglich von der Bereitschaft ihres Herzens fern; damit erreichen sie nur, dass die Pfosten weiter auseinanderstehen, und verwirken so das Leben, das das enge Tor schenkt. Nur wenige werden die Glückseligkeit innerhalb der Pfosten finden.

Diese werden Leben finden innerhalb der von Gott bestimmten Grenzen des engen und schmalen Weges und…

…Regierungen

Die demütige Bitte des Hauptmanns von Kapernaum ließ Jesus staunen –…Wahrlich, ich sage euch: Einen so großen Glauben habe ich selbst in Israel nicht gefunden –Matthäus 8:10. Er war ein Mann mit Vollmacht … und unter Vollmacht. Er schien den Zusammenhang zwischen Unterordnung unter irdische Autorität und deren Ausübung zu verstehen, denn er bat Christus, nicht unter sein Dach zu kommen, sondern …sprich nur ein Wort, und mein Diener wird gesund werden –Matthäus 8:8. Das von seinen Vorgesetzten gesetzte Tor und die aufrichtige Liebe seiner Untergebenen ließen ihm oft nur wenig Raum für persönliche Vorlieben. Doch die in seine Worte verflochtene Vollmacht war so groß, dass der Sohn Gottes seiner Bitte bereitwillig nachkam!

Josef fand sich wiederholt in schwierigen Situationen zwischen Gott und den Menschen, denen er diente. Das führte dazu, dass er zur zweithöchsten Macht im bedeutendsten Staat der Erde erhoben wurde. Ester und Daniel erlebten ähnliche Nöte. Manchmal waren die Pfosten so eng, dass sie sich fragten, ob sie umkommen würden; doch das Ergebnis war immer Macht … Macht, heilig zu leben, Macht, gerecht zu reagieren, Macht, siegreich zu überwinden, und Macht, bis zum Ende treu auszuharren.

…Vorgesetzte

Obwohl die Sklaverei in unserer modernen Welt weitgehend abgeschafft worden ist, besteht das Verhältnis zu einem Herrn weiterhin. Arbeitgeber üben Autorität über ihre Beschäftigten aus, und größere Verantwortung wird letztlich denen übertragen, die sich ihr von ganzem Herzen unterordnen. Die Vollmacht, die Eleasar übertragen wurde, ist erstaunlich und inspirierend. Abraham vertraute ihm an, eine Frau für Isaak zu finden; ihm wurde sogar gestattet, die Regeln festzulegen. Diese gewaltige Verpflichtung brachte den dienstverpflichteten Knecht in eine enge Lage zwischen dem Herrn Gott und seinem Herrn Abraham. Und er sagte: O HERR, Gott meines Herrn Abraham, lass es mir heute doch gelingen und erweise meinem Herrn Abraham Güte –1. Mose 24:12.

Die amerikanische Arbeiterschaft hat sich sehr daran gewöhnt, alles abzulehnen, was sie als unzumutbare Anweisung ihrer Arbeitgeber ansieht. In treulosem Trotz streikt sie bereitwillig und rückt die Pfosten weiter auseinander, bis sie ihren breiten Vorlieben entsprechen. Diese Haltung hat sie geistlich geschwächt und machtlos gemacht. Der äthiopische Kämmerer diente Gott und stand zugleich im Dienst der Königin Kandake. Obwohl seine Welt enger begrenzt war, als die meisten von uns es sich je vorstellen könnten, …zog er voller Freude seines Weges –Apostelgeschichte 8:39. Sein Leben ist ein herausragendes Zeugnis für die Prophezeiung Jesajas …Auch sage der Verschnittene nicht: Siehe, ich bin ein dürrer Baum –Jesaja 56:3.

…Eltern

Ihr Kinder, gehorcht euren Eltern im Herrn, denn das ist recht. Ehre deinen Vater und deine Mutter – das ist das erste Gebot mit einer Verheißung –, damit es dir wohl ergehe und du lange auf der Erde lebst –Epheser 6:1-3. Das sollte jedem geistlich erwachten Menschen klar sein. Kinder, die Eltern haben, haben einen offensichtlichen Vorteil im Leben, und denen, die sie achten, ergeht es noch besser. Außerdem hatten wir leibliche Väter, die uns zurechtwiesen, und wir erwiesen ihnen Achtung. Sollten wir uns dann nicht vielmehr dem Vater der Geister unterordnen und leben? –Hebräer 12:9. Leben finden diejenigen, die ihre irdischen Väter und den „Vater der Geister“ annehmen können. Wer Gott als Vater bekennt, seine Eltern aber als bloßes Hindernis auf dem Weg betrachtet, den er gehen möchte, wird früher oder später durch das breite Tor ins Verderben gehen.

…Ehemänner

Als Jesus am Jakobsbrunnen mit der Samariterin ins Gespräch kam, begann er ein Leben zu beschreiben, nach dem sie sich sehnlichst sehnte –…Herr, gib mir dieses Wasser, damit ich nicht dürste und nicht hierherkommen muss, um zu schöpfen. Jesus sagt zu ihr: Geh, ruf deinen Mann und komm hierher –Johannes 4:16. Christus wollte sie davon überzeugen, dass das Leben in Fülle zwischen den beiden Pfosten zu finden ist. Sie hatte zuvor fünf Männer gehabt und hatte zweifellos bei keinem von ihnen Erfüllung gefunden. Frauen, die für ihre Rechte eintreten, treten gegen die Enge des Tores und verwirken ihre von Gott bestimmte Würde. Eine Frau, die innerhalb der Grenzen ihrer Autoritäten zur Ruhe kommt, wird nicht unterdrückt, sondern tatsächlich befreit und gestärkt. Darum soll die Frau Vollmacht auf ihrem Haupt haben… –1. Korinther 11:10. Die Kopfbedeckung als Zeichen der Hauptschaft ist nicht nur ein Symbol der Unterordnung und auch nicht bloß eine Form des Schutzes; sie ist geistliche Kraft. Ihre uneingeschränkte Unterordnung beflügelt eine lebendige Ehe, während sie ihren Mann als „Herrn“ annimmt; und dadurch wird sie zu einem treuen Gefäß der Freiheit, Macht, Stärke und übertragenen Einflussnahme.

…Gemeindeleiter

Rede über diese Dinge, ermahne und weise mit aller Vollmacht zurecht. Niemand verachte dich –Titus 2:15. Viele selbsternannte Gläubige lehnen jede sichtbare Ausübung von Autorität in der Gemeinde ab. Im westlichen Denken wird kirchliche Autorität negativ mit Gesetzlichkeit, Kommunismus, Knechtschaft und Beschwerlichkeit verbunden. Doch so wie die Missachtung geistlicher Autoritäten Saul seiner Königswürde beraubte, nimmt diese Haltung auch dem Gläubigen wahre autoritative Kraft und Würde. Auflehnung ist wie die Sünde der Zauberei, und Widerspenstigkeit wie Frevel und Götzendienst… –1. Samuel 15:23. Der Versuch, …einen Weg, der einem Menschen richtig erscheint… –Sprüche 14:12, zu wählen, führt in Knechtschaft; wer aber wählt, in Hingabe und Unterordnung zu gehen, gelangt zu Befreiung und Leben. Satan versprach Jesus die ganze Welt, wenn er nur das „Joch“ des Gehorsams gegenüber Gott abwerfen würde. Stattdessen richtete er sein Angesicht wie einen Kieselstein, ertrug die Einschränkung der Unterordnung und befreite letztlich die ganze Welt.

Unterordnung bringt geistliche Vollmacht hervor

Gottes Autorität und irdische Autoritäten wurzeln in den einander gegenüberliegenden Pfosten des engen Tores. Wer sich beiden völlig unterordnet, erfährt eine lebendige Vollmacht, die sich im Tor findet. Sie gibt Menschen Macht, statt Macht über Menschen auszuüben. Sie bringt Freiheit in Christus … das Recht am Baum des Lebens … Befreiung von Furcht … Gesundheit für unsere Gebeine … Macht über unreine Geister … Gnade, Kinder zu erziehen … Kraft, zu predigen und Seelen zu bekehren … und ist das wirksamste Mittel gegen Gesetzlichkeit. Der Glaube, der aus uneingeschränkter und demütiger Unterordnung hervorgeht, ist die am meisten angezweifelte und unterschätzte Kraft, die der Menschheit zur Verfügung steht. Wenige sind es, die ihn finden. Warum? Weil er sorgfältig zwischen den Pfosten des engen Tores und des schmalen Weges begründet und geformt wird.

As a young man I remember hearing a popular slogan about faith: “Faith begins when reason ends.” As a young Christian, I thought it was a great life slogan. As I mature in my walk with Jesus, I look back on this particular slogan and shake my head. I can think of no better way to misrepresent faith than by claiming it exists apart from reason.

One simple reason for rejecting this view is because it misrepresents faith. A quick search on Google turns up this definition of faith: “complete trust or confidence in someone or something.” We use this definition all the time. I might tell you I have faith in my wife, I have faith in my employer to give me a paycheck, or I have no faith in alcohol to give me a good time. This is the same way the Bible defines faith.

Hebrews 11:1 affirms that faith is “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” Biblical faith is simply a state of mind that has confidence and trust in the Lord. I have confidence that I will one day walk on the new Earth, and I have confidence that the Holy Spirit is working in the hearts of Christians. My confidence is based on, not apart from, reason. The more Jesus shows himself trustworthy, the more I trust (have confidence in) Him.

One aspect of Christ’s dependability is His word. The Old Testament was written by prophets and leaders who correctly predicted future events and ruled nations. The New Testament was written by Apostles or people that were closely associated with the apostles. We have more manuscripts of the Bible than any other work in antiquity. The Bible gives an honest portrayal of its heroes and correctly describes ancient leaders and places. In short, I trust in the Bible because it stands alone above all other books in terms of its authorship, preservation, honesty, and accuracy. The more I read it and read about it, the more my faith—and trust—increases.

Luke bases his whole Gospel on the premise that more knowledge gives more faith. He begins his book with this introduction: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled [or been surely believed] among us, just as they were handed down to us by those who from the first were eyewitnesses and servants of the word. With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught. –Luke 1:1-4. (NIV)

The apostle Paul argues that faith in God is so grounded in reality that no one has a legitimate claim against God’s existence. He writes, The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse –Romans 1:18-20. (NIV)

Knowledge of nature builds my faith in Jesus. Scripture teaches that God created all life in six days, that there was a global flood, and that animals produce after their own kind. All across our earth, the rocks cry out their testimony of the global flood. People have uncovered billions of fossils—mostly marine animals—in rock layers that were laid down by water. Animals too, live out what the Bible teaches about kinds. We can observe animals changing all around us. They change sizes, colors, and eating habits. Fish in caves lose their ability to see. Birds’ beaks adjust to the environment. In all this intricate change, all animals exist within the Biblical framework of their own kind. Sharks remain sharks; frogs remain frogs; iguanas remain iguanas; and gibbons remain gibbons. The more I learn and observe about nature, the more my faith (confidence) increases.

In some discussions of faith, it is natural for the words of Jesus to come up. After His resurrection, Jesus visits Thomas and tells him, …Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed –John 20:29. (ESV) From this, it is tempting to define faith as “believing without seeing.” That would be missing the point. I’m not claiming any superiority to Thomas, but he should have believed without seeing Jesus. All the evidence pointed to it. First, his good friends, who had proved themselves trustworthy, said Jesus was alive. Second, Jesus had plainly said He would be resurrected (see Matthew 16:21). Third, Jesus had already proven He was divine by His ability to raise the dead, control the weather, heal the sick, and multiply food. Thomas had all he needed to believe Jesus rose from the dead. Yet, he went against all reasoning and said he needed more evidence.

When confronted with the resurrected Christ, Thomas repented of his disbelief and followed Christ into martyrdom. Unfortunately, the spirit of disbelief in the face of evidence still lingers in our world. Atheists claim, in spite of all evidence to the contrary, that life can come from nothing. They claim, without any evidence, that fish turned into frogs. They blindly cling to various theories such as: The Big Bang, Punctuated Equilibrium, and Descent with Modification. They have NO workable evidence, yet they still claim to base all their thoughts on observable, repeatable reality. Christians, who with good intentions, tell them that faith begins where reason ends, unwittingly play right into their hands. This world does not need a social media definition of faith. They need to see faith for what it is: confidence in the living God based firmly in reason.

أتذكر، حين كنت شابًا، أنني سمعت شعارًا شائعًا عن الإيمان: «يبدأ الإيمان حين ينتهي العقل». وبوصفي مسيحيًا شابًا، ظننت أنه شعار عظيم للحياة. ومع نضجي في سيري مع يسوع، أنظر إلى هذا الشعار بعينه وأهز رأسي استنكارًا. ولا أستطيع أن أتصور طريقة أفضل لتحريف معنى الإيمان من الادعاء بأنه يوجد بمعزل عن العقل.

من الأسباب البسيطة لرفض هذا الرأي أنه يحرّف معنى الإيمان. ويُظهر بحث سريع على غوغل هذا التعريف للإيمان: «الثقة الكاملة بشخص أو بشيء». ونستخدم هذا التعريف طوال الوقت. فقد أقول لك إن لديَّ ثقة بزوجتي، أو إن لديَّ ثقة بأن يمنحني صاحب عملي راتبي، أو إنني لا أثق بالكحول كي يمنحني وقتًا ممتعًا. وهذا هو التعريف نفسه الذي يقدمه الكتاب المقدس للإيمان.

تؤكد عبرانيين 11:1 أن الإيمان هو «الثقة بما نرجوه، واليقين بما لا نراه». والإيمان الكتابي ببساطة حالة ذهنية تتسم بالثقة والاتكال على الرب. لديَّ ثقة بأنني سأمشي يومًا ما على الأرض الجديدة، ولديَّ ثقة بأن الروح القدس يعمل في قلوب المسيحيين. إن ثقتي مبنية على العقل، لا بمعزل عنه. وكلما أظهر يسوع أنه جدير بالثقة، ازددت ثقةً به (واتكالًا عليه).

ومن جوانب اعتمادنا على المسيح كلمته. كتب العهد القديم أنبياء وقادة تنبؤوا بالمستقبل تنبؤًا صحيحًا وحكموا أممًا. أما العهد الجديد فكتبه رسل أو أشخاص ارتبطوا ارتباطًا وثيقًا بالرسل. ولدينا مخطوطات للكتاب المقدس أكثر من أي عمل آخر من أعمال العصور القديمة. ويقدم الكتاب المقدس تصويرًا صادقًا لأبطاله، ويصف القادة والأماكن القديمة وصفًا دقيقًا. باختصار، أثق بالكتاب المقدس لأنه يتفرد بالتفوق على جميع الكتب الأخرى من حيث مؤلفيه، وحفظه، وصدقه، ودقته. وكلما قرأته وقرأت عنه، ازداد إيماني—وثقتي—رسوخًا.

يبني لوقا إنجيله كله على فرضية أن ازدياد المعرفة يزيد الإيمان. ويبدأ كتابه بهذه المقدمة: «إذ كان كثيرون قد أخذوا بتأليف قصة في الأمور المتيقنة عندنا، كما سلّمها إلينا الذين كانوا منذ البدء شهود عيان وخدامًا للكلمة، رأيت أنا أيضًا، بعدما تتبعت كل شيء من الأول بتدقيق، أن أكتب على التوالي إليك أيها العزيز ثاوفيلس، لتعرف صحة الكلام الذي عُلّمت به ويقينه». –لوقا 1:1-4. (NIV)

يجادل الرسول بولس بأن الإيمان بالله راسخ في الواقع إلى حد لا يملك معه أحد حجة مشروعة ضد وجود الله. فهو يكتب: «لأن غضب الله معلن من السماء على جميع فجور الناس وإثمهم، الذين يحجزون الحق بالإثم، إذ معرفة الله ظاهرة فيهم، لأن الله أظهرها لهم. لأن أموره غير المنظورة تُرى منذ خلق العالم مدركة بالمصنوعات، قدرته السرمدية ولاهوته، حتى إنهم بلا عذر». –رومية 1:18-20. (NIV)

إن معرفة الطبيعة تعزز إيماني بيسوع. يعلّم الكتاب المقدس أن الله خلق كل حياة في ستة أيام، وأن طوفانًا عالميًا وقع، وأن الحيوانات تتكاثر بحسب أجناسها. وفي أرجاء أرضنا كلها، تصرخ الصخور بشهادتها عن الطوفان العالمي. وقد اكتشف الناس مليارات الأحافير—معظمها لحيوانات بحرية—في طبقات صخرية ترسبت بفعل الماء. وتعيش الحيوانات أيضًا بحسب ما يعلّمه الكتاب المقدس عن الأجناس. يمكننا أن نلاحظ الحيوانات وهي تتغير من حولنا. فهي تتغير في أحجامها وألوانها وعاداتها الغذائية. وتفقد الأسماك في الكهوف قدرتها على الرؤية. وتتأقلم مناقير الطيور مع البيئة. ومع كل هذه التغيرات الدقيقة، تظل جميع الحيوانات ضمن إطار أجناسها كما يحدده الكتاب المقدس. تظل أسماك القرش أسماك قرش؛ والضفادع ضفادع؛ والإغوانا إغوانا؛ والجيبون جيبونًا. وكلما تعلمت أكثر عن الطبيعة وتأملتها، ازداد إيماني (وثقتي).

في بعض النقاشات حول الإيمان، من الطبيعي أن تُذكر كلمات يسوع. فبعد قيامته، زار يسوع توما وقال له: «لأنك رأيتني يا توما آمنت! طوبى للذين آمنوا ولم يروا». –يوحنا 20:29. (ESV) ومن هذا، يسهل أن نعرّف الإيمان بأنه «التصديق من دون رؤية». لكن ذلك يفوّت المغزى. لا أدّعي أنني أفضل من توما، لكنه كان ينبغي أن يؤمن من دون أن يرى يسوع. فقد أشارت إليه كل الأدلة. أولًا، قال أصدقاؤه المقربون، الذين أثبتوا أنهم جديرون بالثقة، إن يسوع حي. ثانيًا، كان يسوع قد قال بوضوح إنه سيقوم من بين الأموات (انظر متى 16:21). ثالثًا، كان يسوع قد أثبت ألوهيته بالفعل بقدرته على إقامة الموتى، والتحكم في الطقس، وشفاء المرضى، وإكثار الطعام. كان لدى توما كل ما يحتاج إليه ليؤمن بأن يسوع قام من بين الأموات. ومع ذلك، خالف كل استدلال وقال إنه يحتاج إلى مزيد من الأدلة.

حين واجه توما المسيح القائم، تاب عن عدم إيمانه وتبع المسيح حتى الاستشهاد. وللأسف، لا تزال روح عدم التصديق في مواجهة الأدلة عالقة في عالمنا. فالملحدون يزعمون، رغم كل الأدلة المناقضة، أن الحياة يمكن أن تنشأ من لا شيء. ويدّعون، من دون أي دليل، أن الأسماك تحولت إلى ضفادع. ويتشبثون عميانًا بنظريات شتى مثل: الانفجار العظيم، والاتزان المتقطع، والنسل مع التعديل. ليست لديهم أي أدلة عملية قابلة للاستخدام، ومع ذلك يواصلون الادعاء بأنهم يبنون أفكارهم كلها على واقع يمكن ملاحظته وتكراره. والمسيحيون الذين يخبرونهم، بحسن نية، أن الإيمان يبدأ حيث ينتهي العقل، يخدمونهم من حيث لا يدرون. لا يحتاج هذا العالم إلى تعريف للإيمان مأخوذ من وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي؛ بل يحتاج إلى أن يرى الإيمان على حقيقته: ثقة بالله الحي، راسخة في العقل.
